observation_summary: The compiler was incorrectly removing 'goog.require' calls from the AST even when those requires were invalid and needed to be preserved for subsequent error reporting. This caused the compiler to fail to report missing namespaces.
reasoning_summary: The fix involved modifying a conditional predicate ('if (provided != null)') to include an additional check ('|| requiresLevel.isOn()'). This is a classic 'Checking' defect where the logic governing whether to perform an action (removing the node from the AST) was missing a necessary condition, leading to incorrect behavior in the control flow.
evidence_used: The bug report states: 'The method processes goog.require calls... If the require symbol is valid, the method removes it from the ast... the second condition (requiresLevel.isOn()) is invalid and always causes removing of the requires when we want to check these requires.'
The fix diff shows: 'if (provided != null) {' changed to 'if (provided != null || requiresLevel.isOn()) {'

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the logic is procedural, the root cause is specifically a missing condition in a guard clause, which is the definition of a Checking defect.
